Deployments › New app

New app

About this page

The console creates the repository samclement/<name> from the stack's template, waits for its first image, then opens a pull request that adds it to staging. Nothing changes on the cluster until you merge that PR; after that, every push to the repository's main deploys to staging. How it works

1 What you are building

The type sets everything the template includes, and who can reach the app at first. Each can change later.

Type
What each includes: Browser frontend a page built with Vite+ that the app serves at /, calling its own /api; SQLite a database file the platform keeps on a volume and backs up nightly; API description an OpenAPI document of its routes, so other apps can find and call it; Events an AsyncAPI document of the events it publishes, with an example event; Feature flags an example feature flag, set per environment from the console.

2 The app

Its name, the stack it is built from and the team that owns it.

The repository samclement/<name> (it must not exist yet), the image and the namespace <name>-staging.
Stack
Templates: samclement/swhurl-app-template-typescript, samclement/swhurl-app-template-kotlin.
Optional. One line, for the repository, its README and its API description.
Owning team
Choose one: there is no default. A label saying who owns the app: it groups and filters the Deployments list and map, and is on the app's logs and traces as swhurl.team. It does not grant or restrict anyone's access. Add a team or give one a notification channel on the Teams page; an app's team changes later with the app page's Change team.

3 Who can reach it

Its web address in staging, and who may open it. An API is private: browsers reach it through a web app that calls it.

Access

3 Who can reach it

A worker has no web address: it is private, and no other app can connect to it.

4 Connects to optional

The apps it calls and the events it receives. Change these later on the app's page. To publish events, edit the app's asyncapi.yaml.

Connections
Apps it calls
The new app gets each one's address and a short-lived token only that app accepts; each one starts admitting it. Any other app is blocked. Web apps in staging are offered; the catalogue shows each one's routes and each event's payload.
Events it receives
The new app may read exactly these, from the oldest event still kept (seven days).

Choosing a call or a subscription also changes the other app, so the pull request waits for your review instead of merging itself.

What happens

About three minutes, shown step by step on the job page. Production comes later, with Promote to prod.

  1. RepositoryCreates the public repository samclement/<name> from the stack's template.
  2. First buildChecks the app and publishes ghcr.io/samclement/<name>.
  3. Pull requestAdds <name>/staging here, set up from what the image itself declares and what you chose under Connects to: the apps it calls start admitting it, and it gets a key for its events. It waits for your review.
  4. After you mergeEvery push to the app's main deploys to staging.
Creates a real public repository; nothing changes on the cluster until you merge the pull request.
